leads.summary: An existing imv.desktop symlink to the shipped launcher blocks the migration queue
leads.consequence: The -f guard accepts a symlink to $OMARCHY_PATH/applications/imv.desktop, but cp recognizes source and destination as the same file and exits 1. bin/omarchy-migrate:5,84-87 then stops before writing this migration's marker or running any subsequent migration. Retrying the update repeats the same failure until the link is removed or the migration is changed to skip same-file links. The launcher already has the new MIME types in this case.
leads.triage: dropped: requires a manual symlink into OMARCHY_PATH; no Omarchy tooling creates one (coordinator rg over head); same class as N2

leads.summary: The scoped migration still overwrites edited and symlink-managed user launchers
leads.consequence: For an existing customized regular imv.desktop, cp replaces the user's Name, Exec, visibility and any additional MimeType values. For a symlink to a user-maintained desktop file, cp follows the link and overwrites the actual dotfile target. With success, the cache is rebuilt and the migration is marked done, so rerunning does not restore customizations. This fixes the prior migration's broad impact on unrelated launchers but leaves this launcher vulnerable. Preserve custom imv.desktop entries, or update only the needed MIME associations without following user-managed links.

leads.summary: An alternate XDG_DATA_HOME keeps the stale imv registration
leads.consequence: If an existing user has moved their imv.desktop and mimeinfo.cache to a non-default XDG_DATA_HOME, the migration checks and updates only $HOME/.local/share/applications. In a synthetic custom data home, the migration succeeds without changing the active launcher or its cache; `gio mime image/heic` still resolves the explicit system default to imv.desktop, but lists no recommended applications. Refreshing the active custom-data directory makes imv.desktop appear as recommended. Thus the original GIO-registration repair is skipped for these users and a successful one-shot migration marker prevents retry. Use the effective XDG_DATA_HOME (with $HOME/.local/share as fallback) for guard, destination and cache rebuild.
leads.triage: dropped: repo hardcodes ~/.local/share/applications everywhere, incl. omarchy-refresh-applications

leads.summary: Open #13123's imv-dir defaults test rejects the four new image defaults
leads.consequence: #13123 (open, diverged, GitHub mergeable against its own base) changes the six preexisting image defaults to imv-dir.desktop and adds test/shell.d/mimeapps-test.sh asserting every image/* default uses imv-dir.desktop. This PR adds four image/* defaults using imv.desktop. A three-way merge of the two default files has conflict markers. Resolving by retaining both changes makes that PR's unmodified test exit 1, and gives the new formats different folder-navigation behavior; whichever lands second must align all image defaults with the intended viewer.
leads.triage: corroborates R2-N1 (Sol also ran #13123 test on a manual union: exit 1)

leads.summary: The migration comment overstates the role of mimeinfo.cache in GIO defaults
leads.consequence: The comment says GIO reads mimeinfo.cache, not the launcher, and only lists imv for the four types after rebuilding the cache. The cache is needed for recommendations, but GIO also resolves an explicit default from mimeapps.list and loads that desktop file directly. In the stale-cache fixture, `gio mime image/heic` already shows imv.desktop as Default application before rebuilding; its Recommended applications list is what remains empty. Narrow the comment to the registered/recommended-list repair, not default resolution. This is a documentation accuracy lead, not a routing failure.
leads.triage: dropped: comment wording nitpick; Opus confirmed rebuild needed for registered lists

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found.

**Earlier points** (follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12368#issuecomment-5859285563) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12368#issuecomment-5861765022), at `55281c7`):
- **Migration restored removed preinstall launchers and reset edited stock launchers and wrappers: resolved.** It now refreshes only an existing user `imv.desktop` (edits to that file are still lost, see the optional note) and rebuilds `mimeinfo.cache`.
- **`.heic` through `xdg-open`, and GIO registration on existing installs: still resolved.**
- **Related open PR #13123: still applies.** It also conflicts textually in `default/applications/mimeapps.list`. Whichever lands second needs all `image/*` defaults on one launcher.

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- Existing install after Remove > Preinstalls: the migration changed only `imv.desktop` and `mimeinfo.cache` (plus its marker). No launcher was restored and nothing was written to `~/.local/bin`.
- After the migration, GIO lists imv as registered and recommended for AVIF, HEIF, HEIC and JXL. Copying the file without `update-desktop-database` did not, so the rebuild is needed.
- Without a user `imv.desktop` the migration does nothing, and a second run through `omarchy-migrate` changes nothing.
- `xdg-open` and `gio open` send real `.heic`, `.heif` (heic and mif1 brands), `.avif`, `.jxl` and `.png` samples to imv (the mif1 `.heif` is `heif-enc` output with its brand patched). Without the two `image/heic` entries, `xdg-open` sends `.heic` to another viewer (negative control).
- The filename sorts before eight newer base migrations. `omarchy-migrate` runs every unmarked migration, so installs that already ran those still get this one.
</details>

<details><summary>#13123 conflict</summary>

PR #13123 is open at head `c5644eb496faac8058bdff3d1247ac850a627635` (last updated 2026-09-24). Merging it with this PR head in any clone that has both commits (`git fetch https://github.com/omacom/omarchy.git pull/12368/head pull/13123/head` first):

Beyond the text conflict, #13123 adds `test/shell.d/mimeapps-test.sh`, which requires every `image/*` default to be `imv-dir.desktop` and fails on any `image/...=imv.desktop` line, so the four lines this PR adds would fail it until aligned. Source-read only; that test was not executed.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional note: an edited imv.desktop is replaced</summary>

The narrowed migration (the code the earlier review suggested) still copies the stock launcher over an existing user `imv.desktop`. That drops edits such as `Exec=imv-dir %F` or `NoDisplay=true`, and writes through a symlink into a dotfiles directory. Repository precedent `1787580187` (Docker.desktop) behaves the same way, so this is optional. A tested alternative appends the four types only when the `MimeType` line still matches the old stock line:

```bash
echo "Register imv for AVIF, HEIF, HEIC, and JXL"

# Append the new types only to an unmodified stock MimeType line, so other
# edits to the launcher (Exec, NoDisplay, a custom type list) are kept.
dest="$HOME/.local/share/applications/imv.desktop"
stock="MimeType=image/png;image/jpeg;image/jpg;image/gif;image/bmp;image/webp;image/tiff;image/x-xcf;image/x-portable-pixmap;image/x-xbitmap;"
if [[ -f $dest ]] && grep -qxF "$stock" "$dest"; then
  sed -i --follow-symlinks "s|^$stock\$|${stock}image/avif;image/heif;image/heic;image/jxl;|" "$dest"
  update-desktop-database "$HOME/.local/share/applications"
fi
```

In throwaway homes this gave a launcher byte-identical to the PR's for the stock case and registered imv for `image/avif`. A second run changed nothing. It kept `Exec` and `NoDisplay` edits, left a custom `MimeType` line untouched, and worked through a dotfiles symlink.

Reproducer for the current behaviour:

Reproduced at PR head `55281c781db05e9148403f0a683a74494778d87c`, run with bash 5.3.15, coreutils 9.11 and desktop-file-utils 0.28 in a throwaway HOME. Usage: `bash repro-edited-launcher.sh /path/to/omarchy-checkout-at-PR-head`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Reproducer: migration 1789706522 replaces a user-edited imv.desktop.
# Usage: bash repro-edited-launcher.sh <omarchy checkout at the PR head>
# Uses a throwaway HOME; nothing outside it is written.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1
HOME=$(mktemp -d)
export HOME
apps=$HOME/.local/share/applications
mkdir -p "$apps"

# The launcher as shipped before this PR (the PR's line minus the four new types),
# then two common user edits: open the whole folder, and hide it from the launcher.
sed 's#image/avif;image/heif;image/heic;image/jxl;##' "$repo/applications/imv.desktop" >"$apps/imv.desktop"
sed -i 's#^Exec=imv %F$#Exec=imv-dir %F#' "$apps/imv.desktop"
echo 'NoDisplay=true' >>"$apps/imv.desktop"

echo "== before"
grep -E '^(Exec|NoDisplay)=' "$apps/imv.desktop"
OMARCHY_PATH=$repo bash -euo pipefail "$repo/migrations/1789706522.sh"
echo "== after"
grep -E '^(Exec|NoDisplay)=' "$apps/imv.desktop" || true
```

Actual output:

```text
== before
Exec=imv-dir %F
NoDisplay=true
Refresh imv launcher so it registers for AVIF, HEIF, HEIC, and JXL
== after
Exec=imv %F
```

The same happens when `imv.desktop` is a symlink into a dotfiles directory: `cp` writes through the link and the dotfile itself gets the stock content.
</details>
